# Braising basics

Braising means browning meat hard, then cooking it low and slow in a little liquid under a lid. Shoulder of lamb, short ribs and pork cheeks all love it, because the collagen needs hours to melt into the sauce. Season the meat the day before, dry it well and brown it in batches so the pot never steams.

Deglaze with wine, add stock, a handful of aromatics and put the pot in a 150 degree oven. Check after two hours: the meat should yield to a spoon. Rest it in its liquid, skim the fat and reduce the sauce on the hob until it coats the back of a spoon.

Braises improve overnight, so cook them a day ahead.
